title: "Setup"
subtitle: "What to install before the sessions"
number-sections: false
---

You need a working R + Quarto toolchain and an editor. Everything below is standard; if you
already render Quarto documents from R, you are ready.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Setup at a glance
Four steps, top to bottom — each links to its details below:

1. [**Install**](#software) R ≥ 4.5, Quarto ≥ 1.9, and an editor.
2. [**Get the materials**](#get-the-materials) — one line of R, no git or GitHub account needed.
3. [**Install the R packages**](#r-packages) — `renv::restore()` from the project.
4. [**Check it works**](#check-your-setup) — `quarto check` plus a couple of R lines.

Do steps 2–4 **before you arrive** — walking in with the toolchain already in place means we start on the content, not the install.
:::

## Software

- **R ≥ 4.5.0.** The running dataset (`penguins`) ships in base R only since 4.5 — check with
  `R.version.string`. The exercises use the base-R names (`bill_len`, `bill_dep`, …), so R ≥ 4.5
  is the smoothest path; if you truly can't upgrade, see the fallback below.
- **Quarto ≥ 1.9.** Check with `quarto --version`; get it from
  <https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/>. (1.9 is required — the Typst margin/article layout we
  use on Day 1 landed in 1.9.)
- **An editor with Quarto support** — [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/), VS Code (+ the
  Quarto extension), or RStudio. All work; we drive Quarto from the command line too
  (`quarto preview` / `quarto render`), so the editor is your choice.

::: {.callout-tip}
Typst (the modern PDF path we use on Day 1) ships **inside** Quarto — there is nothing extra to
install, no LaTeX.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Stuck on R < 4.5? (dataset fallback)
The exercises assume base R's `penguins`. If you genuinely can't get to R ≥ 4.5, install
[`palmerpenguins`](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/) and rename its columns to the
base-R names the material uses — then every snippet works unchanged:

```r
# install.packages("palmerpenguins")
library(dplyr)
penguins <- palmerpenguins::penguins |>
  rename(
    bill_len    = bill_length_mm,
    bill_dep    = bill_depth_mm,
    flipper_len = flipper_length_mm,
    body_mass   = body_mass_g
  )
```

Run this once at the top of a document (or your session) before the exercise code. Upgrading R is
still the cleaner path if you can.
:::

## Get the materials

The exercises build on files in this repo — starter documents, the completed reference projects, and
the citation assets (`references.bib`, `apa.csl`). The easiest way to get everything — **no git, no
GitHub account, nothing to unzip by hand**, identical on Windows/macOS/Linux — is **`use_course()`**
from R:

```r
# install.packages("usethis")   # once, if you don't have it
usethis::use_course("cderv/raukr-2026-quarto")
```

**What it does**, so nothing surprises you:

1. picks a sensible spot — your **Desktop** by default — and prints where it's about to download. To
   put it elsewhere, cancel and re-run with a path, e.g.
   `use_course("cderv/raukr-2026-quarto", destdir = "~/projects")`.
2. downloads the repo as a ZIP, **unpacks it for you** into a new project folder (it prints the exact
   name), and asks *"Shall we delete the ZIP file?"* — say **yes**.
3. **opens the project** — a new RStudio session, or (in Positron / VS Code) the folder; if it
   doesn't pop open, open the folder it printed yourself.

You land inside the project, with `renv.lock` and every lab file in place. Run the **R packages** and
**Check** steps below **from there** — that folder is the "project root" they refer to.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Prefer git? (optional)
Clone it instead — same files, plus a live link to any updates:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/cderv/raukr-2026-quarto.git
cd raukr-2026-quarto
```

Then open the folder in your editor. The steps below run from the project root either way.
:::

## R packages

This repo pins its R dependencies with [**renv**](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/), so you can
recreate the exact environment. From the repo root:

```r
# install.packages("renv")   # if you don't have it
renv::restore()
```

When you first open the project, renv prints a few bootstrap lines ending in a reminder to run
`renv::restore()` — that's expected, just run it.

That installs the locked versions (`knitr`, `rmarkdown`, `ggplot2`, `dplyr`, `gt`, plus
`brand.yml`, `ggrepel`, `prismatic` for the branded Typst payoff, and their dependencies) into a
project-local library — it won't touch your other R projects.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Not using renv?
You can install the same packages the plain way:

```r
install.packages(c(
  "knitr", "rmarkdown", "ggplot2", "dplyr", "gt",
  "brand.yml", "ggrepel", "prismatic"
))
```

Or with [**pak**](https://pak.r-lib.org/) — same list, but it installs in parallel, prefers
binaries, and sorts out system dependencies for you:

```r
# install.packages("pak")   # once, if you don't have it
pak::pak(c(
  "knitr", "rmarkdown", "ggplot2", "dplyr", "gt",
  "brand.yml", "ggrepel", "prismatic"
))
```
:::

## Check your setup

The single command that proves the whole toolchain — including the **knitr engine** (the `knitr` +
`rmarkdown` packages that a `.qmd` with R code needs) — is:

```sh
quarto check
```

It reports your Quarto version, checks the install, and **renders a small knitr test document**. You
want to see the `knitr` / `rmarkdown` versions and a line reading `Checking Knitr engine
render......OK`. If instead you see `rmarkdown: (None)` (or `The rmarkdown package is not available
in this R installation`), your R packages aren't installed yet — do the [R packages](#r-packages)
step above and re-run.

Then confirm the R side:

```r
R.version.string            # want >= 4.5.0
"penguins" %in% ls("package:datasets")   # want TRUE on R >= 4.5
```

(Your **Quarto** version was already printed by `quarto check` above — or run `quarto --version` in a
terminal.)

::: {.callout-note}
## Pre-warm the Typst fonts (once, before the session)
The **first** Typst render downloads the brand's Google fonts (Albert Sans / Fira Mono). Trigger it
once ahead of time — after `renv::restore()` — so the fonts are already cached and your first render
in the session is instant. The simplest way is to render the shipped branded sample:

```sh
quarto render labs/quarto/sample-typst.qmd
```

Non-blocking: if you skip it, the first render at the session just takes a little longer (given a
network connection).
:::
